scope: Every intentional protocol, ownership, identity, placement, rendering, input, selection, session, or X-server-resource translation that prevents a literal X11 implementation on native Wayland.

entries.summary: X icon windows and pixmaps become compositor-owned icon scenes.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Rootless Xwayland cannot transplant an arbitrary client-owned X window into a Wayland scene, and native xdg-shell has no standard icon-window request.

entries.summary: twm menus become a compositor-owned scene layer.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland compositors own composition and cannot reproduce twm's client-side X menu windows as literal root children.

entries.summary: Refresh actions damage and repaint compositor-owned scene content.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland has no X root-window exposure event that a compositor can send to native clients.

entries.summary: The X cut buffer is mirrored through the Wayland CLIPBOARD selection.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Native Wayland has no global X-style root cut-buffer property.

entries.summary: X11 clients run through a compositor-owned rootless Xwayland server.
entries.unavoidable_reason: A Wayland compositor does not manage an existing X server root and must bridge X11 clients through Xwayland.

entries.summary: Fractional output coordinates use deterministic shared-edge rounding.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland output scale is expressed in logical coordinates and 120ths rather than X screen pixels.

entries.summary: Identify and version output is written to the compositor log.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland has no server-owned X information window in which to display the result.

entries.summary: Restart and twmrc reload use one atomic in-process transaction.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Replacing the compositor process would destroy accepted Wayland resources, focus, selections, and Xwayland ownership.

entries.summary: Legacy bell and XSync priority behavior is conditional at the protocol boundary.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Native Wayland defines neither a compositor bell request nor twm's XSync priority control.

entries.summary: Physical input devices are aggregated into one logical Wayland seat.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland exposes input capabilities and focus through logical seats rather than twm's direct X device model.

entries.summary: Native delete and destroy actions both issue xdg-shell close requests.
entries.unavoidable_reason: xdg-shell has no protocol operation that forcibly disconnects only one arbitrary native client.

entries.summary: Colormap rotation is a verified no-op for native clients.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Native true-color Wayland buffers expose neither WM_COLORMAP_WINDOWS nor an installed-colormap protocol.

entries.summary: Native initial placement selects an output from pointer or parent state.
entries.unavoidable_reason: xdg-shell supplies no X11 USPosition/PPosition hints and no blocking root placement grab.

entries.summary: Native application popups retain their validated xdg parent hierarchy.
entries.unavoidable_reason: xdg-shell popups are parented protocol objects rather than independent X override-redirect root children.

entries.summary: Native resizing uses the subset of size constraints exposed by xdg-shell.
entries.unavoidable_reason: xdg-shell exposes minimum and maximum size but not X11 base, increment, or aspect hints.

entries.summary: Native window-list matching maps X name, instance, and class identity to title and app_id.
entries.unavoidable_reason: xdg-shell exposes title and app_id but has no independent WM_CLASS instance and class pair.

entries.summary: Each enabled output box is a spatial root equivalent and the compositor paints its background.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland outputs are not independent X screens with server-owned root windows, and the compositor owns every output pixel.

entries.summary: Native popups and Xwayland override-redirect surfaces share a map-ordered overlay.
entries.unavoidable_reason: An X ConfigureNotify has no native-surface identity and cannot express sibling order across protocol families.

entries.summary: Session restoration uses an explicit compositor-owned state snapshot.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Native Wayland has no WM_SAVE_YOURSELF or X session-manager restart/discard property protocol.

entries.summary: The screen-zero configuration is one global configuration for all outputs.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland outputs are not separate X screens with independently parsed root configurations.

entries.summary: Wayland CLIPBOARD and PRIMARY offers bridge to X11 selections under seat-focus rules.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland transfers selections with focused-seat offers and file descriptors rather than X owner windows, target atoms, and properties.

entries.summary: A safe f.startwm self-handoff becomes an atomic in-process restart.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Wayland offers no generic transfer of accepted client resources to an arbitrary replacement compositor process.

entries.summary: Non-ASCII decoration text falls back from X core fonts to bounded Pango rendering.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Native Wayland has no X core font server or XLFD glyph protocol for general Unicode text.

entries.summary: Backing-store, save-under, and global-server-grab controls are verified no-ops.
entries.unavoidable_reason: Those resources are properties of X server windows and grabs and do not exist in a Wayland compositor scene graph.
